findings.title: Base-case timeout and infrastructure exceptions are reported as completed observations
findings.claim: The frozen mapping groups every rc=4 with a genuine failed assertion. CURRENT chay_ca catches TimeoutExpired and FileNotFoundError as rc=4. Thus a timed-out base case becomes hoan_tat/failed and ket_luan_tong=do, while the same execution failure in a mutant/TU_KIEM becomes timed_out or infrastructure_error. This violates plan r4 A+3's separation of execution from observation. K5 requires tests to affirm the wrong base-case row, and its timeout/infrastructure fixtures can be satisfied using only mutants.

manifestations.description: TimeoutExpired during a base case becomes hoan_tat/failed.

evidence.observed: CASE timeout (4, "HONG:probe:TimeoutExpired: Command 'git' timed out after 60 seconds"); CASE spawn (4, 'HONG:probe:FileNotFoundError: git'); both map under SPEC line 112 to hoan_tat/failed/do. Assertion control returns rc=3. These are actual chay_ca results; SPEC_MAPPING is a literal interpretation of the candidate, not an implementation run.

suggested_fix.where: Revise §4's base-case rows, structured runner result contract, and K5 in SPEC.md; execution information must be retained where chay_ca catches the exception, before the formatter loses it.
suggested_fix.how: Keep legacy mutant classification semantics intact, but carry a separate structured execution outcome for base-case timeout/infrastructure failures. Define which genuine completed test failures remain failed, and make the mapping exhaustive across ca/dot_bien/tu_kiem.

Verify legacy rc/phan_hang behavior independently.
suggested_fix.what_the_fix_may_spawn: Overbroad exception classification could hide an actual assertion or product failure as infrastructure. Extra result fields can break legacy tuple unpacking and the existing self-mutants.
